name: Agamaggan's Strength
summary: In Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth offers Horde travelers Agamaggan's Strength in return for Blood Shards. The captive Razormane shaman draws on his people's reverence for the ancient boar demigod and his hatred of the rival Bristleback tribe.

sections.title: Power of the Great Boar
sections.body: The quilboar honor Agamaggan, an ancient boar demigod whose spilled blood is said to have formed the red Blood Shards scattered across the Barrens. They treat the crystals as sacred, drawing on their power to strengthen their front-line fighters. Mangletooth, an elder Razormane shaman held captive in Camp Taurajo, offers this strength to Horde champions. He claims your foes will cower as they do before the Razormane's mightiest champions.

sections.title: A Bitter Shaman's Vengeance
sections.body: Mangletooth offers his strength out of spite. The orcs and tauren captured and caged the old quilboar, whose Razormane tribe is at war with the rival Bristleback. Unable to break his chains and slaughter them himself, he trades Agamaggan's gifts for help against them. He rewards those who destroy Bristleback tribes and take the sacred Blood Shards from their lands.

faq.answer: Agamaggan's Strength grants enhanced physical prowess through the power of Blood Shards. It lends the recipient the brutal might of the Razormane's fiercest fighters.
Mangletooth is an imprisoned Razormane quilboar held in Camp Taurajo in the southern Barrens. He hates the rival Bristleback and trades quilboar secrets and blessings for Blood Shards.

aliases: where do blood shards come from
faq.answer: Blood Shards are reddish, crystal-like minerals found across the Barrens. Quilboar tradition says they formed where the blood of their patron demigod, the Great Boar Agamaggan, fell during the ancient War of the Ancients.

faq.q: Why does Mangletooth help the Horde?
faq.answer: Mangletooth helps the Horde because he hates the rival Bristleback quilboar. Though caged at Camp Taurajo and abandoned by his own people, he grants Horde champions Agamaggan's blessings if they butcher his rivals and take their sacred Blood Shards.

faq.q: Can you receive this blessing more than once?
faq.answer: Yes. After you complete Mangletooth's introductory trial, he continues to weave Agamaggan's Strength and other boons when you bring him four more Blood Shards.

faq.q: What is the difference between the Bristleback and Razormane tribes?
faq.answer: The Bristleback and Razormane are rival quilboar tribes competing for the Barrens. Mangletooth belongs to the Razormane, despises the Bristleback, and boasts that his tribe is stronger.

angles.text: As a warrior, you can draw on the raw vigor Mangletooth channels from the boar-god for a physical edge in battle across Kalimdor.
Camp Taurajo's guards keep Mangletooth locked up, but Horde commanders exploit the old shaman's thirst for vengeance against hostile quilboar.

As a tauren, you help maintain Camp Taurajo and watch Mangletooth warily. Your shamans recognize Agamaggan as an ancient guardian spirit of the land, though quilboar zealotry has corrupted his memory.
